paragraphs: Friend, Nahum opens with a God who is jealous, avenging and full of wrath, and then he says the LORD is "slow to anger and great in power" (Nahum 1:2-3). Hold both of those at the same time. The patience is real, and so is the justice. Nobody gets to treat God's patience like a snooze button, and I have hit that button more mornings than I will admit.

Right in the middle of the storm and fire, Nahum says, "The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of distress; He cares for those who trust in Him" (Nahum 1:7). The same God who ends Nineveh's plotting is the One who tells Judah, "I will afflict you no longer" (Nahum 1:12). So His justice is not bad news for everybody. For the ones who trust Him, it is the sound of the shackles coming off. He is the solid brick house in the storm, and you can run to Him.

So here is the big idea, baker. God sees the evil that people plot against Him, and He will bring it to an end. He also sees His people under the yoke, and He will break it. Look to the mountains, because Nahum says there are "the feet of one who brings good news, who proclaims peace" (Nahum 1:15). Trust Him today, and you can celebrate like Judah did.
